assignment.acceptance_condition: Proved: child-max >= 3x parent-max off the parent edge; branching <= 3 (root: 1); N(H) <= (3H-1)/2; depth(v) <= log_3 max(v) and depth(v) >= log_3 log max(v) - O(1) with explicit constants; a clearly labeled statement of any sharper proved bound or, failing that, the precise obstruction plus a labeled conjecture. Explicit constants everywhere.
assignment.objective: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous upper bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions with d <= H} and the two-sided depth-vs-log-H relation, ASSUMING the tree structure (prove the per-edge growth and branching lemmas directly so the thread is self-contained where cheap). Compact plan: (i) at a non-root vertex, mutating any of the three non-maximal coordinates x gives a child with new maximum 4*(product of three others) - x >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; hence max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)); the root has exactly one child (1,1,1,3) - verify. (ii) Each non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root exactly 1, so N(H) <= sum_{k=0}^{floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1}-1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H) with explicit constant. (iii) Two-sided depth relation: upper depth bound log_3 H from (i); lower bound from the coarse child estimate d_child <= 4*d^3 (since a,b,c <= d), giving log max(v) <= 3^{depth(v)} * C for an explicit constant C, hence depth(v) >= log_3(log max(v)) - O(1) along every branch; identify along which branches each extreme is approached. (iv) Attempt to sharpen the O(H) constant or exponent rigorously (e.g., exploit that the (1,1,c,d)-chain is the unique slowest branch and off-chain children grow by factor >= 4ab-1 with ab >= 2, so most of the tree grows much faster; try to prove N(H) = O(H^alpha) for some alpha < 1); if a sharper bound cannot be fully proved, state exactly what is proved, and label any improvement as CONJECTURE with the precise gap. KEEP COMPACT (well under 1200 words): theorems with terse proofs, explicit constants, no tables.

context.product_intent: This run tests mathematical discovery and proof, not research composition: the memorandum exists to establish from first principles, with complete proofs, what is true about the Markov-Hurwitz n=4 mutation graph and the growth of solution counts N(H), with theorems cleanly separated from labeled, reproducible observations and from conjecture. Honest partial progress with clearly stated obstructions — and no assumed growth law — is the explicit acceptance standard, so the product's value lies in rigor and in identifying the most informative next mathematical step.

context.task: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
context.title: Markov-Hurwitz equation a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd: Vieta-mutation graph structure and growth of N(H)
